articles.title: How we built a shopping MCP server with OAuth on Next.js and Vercel
articles.excerpt: Deal.ai is an AI shopping agent: it compares the same product's price across US stores, keeps each product's price history, and checks whether a deal's "was" price holds up. This month we made it usab…
articles.body: Deal.ai is an AI shopping agent: it compares the same product's price across US stores, keeps each product's price history, and checks whether a deal's "was" price holds up. This month we made it usable inside Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code as a remote MCP server at https://deal.ai/mcp . It's now listed in Claude's connectors directory and ChatGPT's plugin directory . The tools were the easy part. Most of the work went into three things: sign-in for people who will never paste an API key, tools that take minutes rather than milliseconds, and getting through directory reviews. Here's how it fits together on Next.js and Vercel, and what we learned. Disclosure: I'm the CTO of Deal.ai.

articles.title: Designing Inclusive Mobile Apps: Accessibility Done Right
articles.excerpt: Designing Inclusive Mobile Apps: Accessibility Beyond Just Contrast Ratios When developers hear "accessibility," they often think of automated Lighthouse scores or ensuring text has a 4.5:1 contrast r…
articles.body: Designing Inclusive Mobile Apps: Accessibility Beyond Just Contrast Ratios When developers hear "accessibility," they often think of automated Lighthouse scores or ensuring text has a 4.5:1 contrast ratio. While these technical specifications are important, they barely scratch the surface of true inclusive design . Building an accessible mobile app means recognizing that your users are navigating the digital world with varying levels of vision, hearing, motor skills, and cognitive processing. 1. Dynamic Type and Layout Fluidity Many developers hardcode font sizes, assuming users will view the app exactly as it appears in Figma. This completely breaks when a visually impaired user increases their system font size by 200%. Best Practice: Never use fixed heights for text containers.

articles.title: 15 files a café needs before it stops answering “how much?”
articles.excerpt: 15 files a café needs before it stops answering “how much?” A café near me has 214 photos, 4.6 stars and 96 reviews on Google Maps, and no website. Every day somebody stands at the counter and asks tw…
articles.body: 15 files a café needs before it stops answering “how much?” A café near me has 214 photos, 4.6 stars and 96 reviews on Google Maps, and no website. Every day somebody stands at the counter and asks two questions the listing cannot answer: how much is a flat white , and are you open on Saturday . The owner answers both about forty times a day. That shop does not need a website builder. It needs a small, boring set of printed things that all point at one live page — the door, the tables, the Wi-Fi card, the delivery apps, the review ask. I build that pack as a product, so I had to decide exactly how many pieces it is and what each one has to contain. The answer came out at 15 items: one live page plus fourteen files.

articles.title: How to Build a Credential Boundary for AI Agents Before They Join a Swarm
articles.excerpt: A coding agent can be told to keep a token private and still hand it to a stranger that promises to help finish the task. That is not just a prompt-writing problem. It is an access-control problem. An…
articles.body: A coding agent can be told to keep a token private and still hand it to a stranger that promises to help finish the task. That is not just a prompt-writing problem. It is an access-control problem. An October 2026 sandbox experiment gave coding agents a broken pricing service and access to a simulated forum. Some forum members offered the fix, but asked newcomers to share environment variables and run an installation script first. In 181 swarm-forum trials, agents posted the private token in 15% and ran the script in 24%. On an ordinary forum that offered the same fix without those conditions, the reported rates were 2% and 0%.

They fail because the client stops knowing what is happening. A week of silence feels like a week of nothing — even when you have been working every day. The client fills the silence with worry, then with doubt, then with a search for your replacement. Good communication is not extra work on top of the project. It is the project, from the client's side of the desk. In the sample, one freelancer lost a $1,850-a-month retainer client — not over quality, but over a 10-day stretch with no update. The work was done. The client just never saw it.

articles.title: Flutter Role-Based Access Control Guide
articles.excerpt: When I built the Muntazim Parent App, a school management app for parents, one requirement shaped the whole architecture: a parent must see only their own child's attendance, grades and fee status, ne…
articles.body: When I built the Muntazim Parent App, a school management app for parents, one requirement shaped the whole architecture: a parent must see only their own child's attendance, grades and fee status, never another family's data. Teachers see their classes, school admins see everything, and parents see exactly one slice. That boundary is role-based access control, and getting it wrong means showing one family another family's private information. Role-based access control (RBAC) is the pattern of grouping permissions into roles and checking those permissions at every layer of the app: the UI hides what a role cannot use, the router blocks routes a role cannot open, and the server rejects requests a role cannot make.

Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona.

articles.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
articles.excerpt: Every November, I give myself a completely unscientific eyesight test using one of my favorite sights in the night sky — the Pleiades. How many stars can you see?
articles.body: Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.excerpt: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
articles.body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
